title: lore check enforces validate's error-tier quote-safety findings, so the two gates cannot disagree (ADR-0007; LCLI-606 carve-out)
description: opum-agent ratified LCLI-606 (R11) as shipped on 2026-09-26T23:39:51Z, on one condition: the quote-safety carve-out must be explained, and filed as a follow-up if it means check and validate can disagree on the same file. They can. lore validate reports error-severity quote-safety findings on AUTHOR-WRITTEN frontmatter scalars that YAML-1.1 consumers read differently (src/core/validate.ts, "frontmatter quote-safety": a bare YYYY-MM-DD date, a bare yes/no/on/off, and YAML indicator characters), while lore check deliberately does not keep them (src/commands/check.ts validateRuleCheckFindings: "Not kept: quote-safety ..."). So a document with an unquoted date can exit 6 under validate and 0 under check: the defect ADR-0007 exists to prevent. Before changing it, measure the fleet by ref (as for LCLI-606 AC2) for error-tier quote-safety findings, since unlike R11 this may have real impact; route any hits to their owners, and treat it as a behaviour change with a CHANGELOG entry.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A fleet measurement by ref of error-tier quote-safety findings (repos read, files read, hits, positive control) is recorded here before the change lands, and any hit is routed to its owner
lore check reports every error-tier quote-safety finding lore validate reports, under the quote-safety rule name, proven by tests that assert the two gates agree on the same file
CHANGELOG marks it a behaviour change naming lore validate as the preview; bun test and bun run lore check exit 0

implementationNotes: AC1 FLEET MEASUREMENT 2026-09-28 ~16:50Z, by ref. Method (LCLI-606 AC2, adapted): each repo's origin/dev was fetched, exported with git archive into scratch, then git init + git add (no commit). lore validate --json ran from lore-cli source at origin/dev e7f20324. The count is findings with rule quote-safety and severity error; warnings were counted separately. REPOS READ: 11 of 11 with parseable JSON: opum-agent 3d4f9feb (17 files), opum-doc f7b549bf (183), lore-cli e7f20324 (82), quest-cli 8342cac9 (63), opum-cli-e2e 4e019125 (7), lore-web a14d6dd0 (13), quest-web 85a0abb4 (14), opum-web 809883cc (4), opum-marketplace 86aee66a (6), opum-fleet a10d004f (6), ward-cli 8b34a314 (1). That is 396 files, and every validate run exited 0. RESULT: 0 error-tier quote-safety findings in every repo, and 0 warning-tier findings too. Nothing needs routing to an owner. POSITIVE CONTROL, same pass: two lines were added to the frontmatter of opum-doc docs/adr/add-a-computed-dotted-display-id-over-quests-flat-canonical-sequence.md, in the export copy only: 'reviewed: 2026-09-28' and 'archived: yes'. validate then exited 6 with an ERROR for the bare yes and only a WARNING for the bare date. lore check on the same modified file exited 0, which reproduces the ADR-0007 disagreement this task exists to remove. The file was restored byte-identical (cmp), and validate re-read 0 errors. CORRECTION to this task's description: a bare YYYY-MM-DD date is WARNING-tier in validate, not error-tier, so only the bare boolean (and the indicator-character cases, per src/core/validate.ts) is in AC2's scope, since AC2 enforces error-tier only.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-28 at commit 2c9fb49a (on d92b89f0), lore from source 0.11.0, bun 1.3.14, quest 0.11.0. DESIGN: no second mechanism. LCLI-606's filter in validateRuleCheckFindings (src/commands/check.ts) now also keeps severity=error rule=quote-safety, so check reports validate's own finding (same rule name, byte-identical message, same repo-relative path + docs-root judge). 'quote-safety' added to CheckRule (src/core/check.ts). Warning-tier quote-safety (bare YYYY-MM-DD date) is NOT kept, not even under --strict. DOUBLE-REPORTING: none; no other check rule reads frontmatter scalar quoting (each positive test asserts exactly one finding for the file). MEASURED BEFORE/AFTER on 13 shapes (validate/check exit): before, archived: yes|off, one: y, alias: :colon, ref: &anchor value were 6/0 (the disagreement); after, all 6/6 with identical findings. RESIDUAL, unchanged and documented: 6 error-tier shapes are also invalid YAML (@x, `x`, !tag x, *x, |foo, 'a: b'). Both gates already exit 6 on them, but check carries the YAML parse error (complete: false + stderr envelope) and runs no per-file rule for that file, so validate's quote-safety finding beside its YAML frontmatter error is not in check's report. Making check report it would change the unparseable-YAML path LCLI-606 left alone; not done here. TESTS: new test/check-quote-safety.test.ts (11) spawns the real CLI (bun src/cli.ts) for check --json and validate --json on the same file: [quote-safety] yes/no/on/off, ':' and '&' indicators, beside a missing type (set = frontmatter + quote-safety), scoped check docs/reference; each asserts both exit 6 and check's findings == validate's error findings (whole set, severity+rule+message). Controls: bare date (validate 0 with a warning-tier quote-safety; check 0, no quote-safety, no error), quoted "yes" (both 0, no quote-safety), 'note: a: b' (both 6; validate frontmatter+quote-safety; check complete:false, no finding for the file, validation envelope naming 'not valid YAML'). test/constitution.test.ts: LCLI-595's 'a quote-safety warning validate raises is NOT reported by check' pinned the old carve-out and misnamed its case (summary: yes is ERROR-tier in validate); split into 'error-tier IS reported, identical to validate's' and 'warning-tier (bare ratified date) is NOT reported, even under --strict'. DOCS: ADR-0007 new dated LCLI-612 amendment (LCLI-606's left as its dated record); cli-surface check bullet + Exit row; cli-contract check.report kind row + exit-6 row; okf-conformance 'Lore-specific gates'. Grep of the bare word quote-safety across docs/ src/ skills/ classified: remaining hits describe validate (architecture, lore-design, tech-stack, ADR-0003/0011/0013, instructions validation topic), are dated history (ADR-0007 LCLI-606 amendment, release-truth, CHANGELOG), or are the new text. CHANGELOG not edited (parent adds at landing).

Restored from a saved copy, cmp exit 0; lore check back to exit 0, 82 files, 0 errors.

LANDING (parent session, 2026-09-28). The parent read the src/ diff of 2c9fb49a: validateRuleCheckFindings keeps severity error with rule quote-safety, and CheckRule gains 'quote-safety'. Nothing else in the logic changes. AC3: CHANGELOG [Unreleased] > Changed carries a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE entry that names lore validate as the preview and marks this a minor-release item. Gates are the implementer's, at 2c9fb49a (bun 1.3.14, lore from source 0.11.0): bun test 4372 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail; bun run lore check exit 0 (82 files). This commit adds the CHANGELOG entry and tracker records only, and CI on the PR head re-runs both. Known residual, documented in the ADR-0007 LCLI-612 amendment: six error-tier shapes are also invalid YAML (@x, a backtick value, !tag x, *x, |foo, a: b). check stops at the parse error for those, with exit 6 as validate, and does not list validate's quote-safety finding beside it. Both gates exit 6 on them, so they cannot disagree on the verdict.
finalSummary: lore check now reports every error-tier quote-safety finding that lore validate reports (bare YAML-1.1 booleans, leading indicator characters, and ': ' inside a value), with the same rule name and byte-identical messages, for every type. check and validate therefore cannot disagree on the same file. That disagreement is the ADR-0007 defect LCLI-606's carve-out left open. Warning-tier quote-safety (a bare date) stays validate-only. A fleet measurement by ref, taken before the change, found 0 affected files: 11 repos, 396 files, with a positive control. Verified by test/check-quote-safety.test.ts, which runs real check and validate on the same file and requires identical findings and exit 6, plus controls. A mutation that removes the rule turned exactly the 9 predicted tests red. Also: bun test 4372/0, and lore check exit 0 with a positive control on this repo. The ADR-0007 amendment, cli-surface, cli-contract, okf-conformance and CHANGELOG (BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, minor release) are updated.
